question: An internal FAQ drafted with help from a project is about to be published to all staff. Which maintenance step matters most before it goes out?
options: A) Confirm the FAQ is long enough to cover every question the team has ever received from staff.
B) Check each answer against the current source documents and confirm none rely on superseded material.
C) Ask Claude to review its own FAQ and to confirm that all of the answers it has written are accurate.
D) Republish the FAQ every month so that errors in the current version are eventually replaced.
correct_answers: B) Check each answer against the current source documents and confirm none rely on superseded material.
explanations: Coverage is not the risk here; answers drawn from outdated sources are.
Correct. Publication is the point at which a stale source turns into a broadly circulated wrong answer.
A self-review cannot detect that the underlying uploaded source was out of date.
Scheduled republication does not stop the first version going out with wrong answers.
